ops.title: No main-path code exists for a test: delete the seams, don't just swap the fakes
ops.body:
Directive from yasyf, 2026-08-02, sharpening the fake removal.

"Make sure you are not ever writing main-path code just for a test."

The repo already states this for one case — design directive D15: `Owned.Ctx` "ships as a
production surface, not a test seam." The rule generalizes: a field, parameter, or interface that
exists so a test can substitute something is production code the product does not use, and it is
exactly what lets a fake attach in the first place. Removing the fake while leaving the socket it
plugged into fixes half the defect.

Measured 2026-08-02: **zero non-test assignments** to `.verify`, `.run`, `.inventory`,
`.launchctl`, or `.probe` anywhere in the module. Production never sets one.

## Test-only seams — delete

- `client.go:42-47` — `Client` carries SIX injectable funcs: `probe`, `observe`, `identities`,
  `readOwner`, `kill`, `serving`. Production sets none.
- `deploy/deploy.go:103,106` — `verify verifier` and `inventory func(...string) (Survivors, error)`.
- `control.go:92` — `observe` on Control.
- `internal/wire/session.go:89,709` — `beforeWrite func()`, a pure test hook.
- `launchd/apply.go:111` — `wait func(context.Context, time.Duration) error`.
- Injectable parameters of the same shape: `ensure.go:413-415` (readOwner, probe, kill),
  `control.go:187-188` (probe, health), `internal/proc/inventory.go:78-80` (list, executable,
  probe), `internal/wire/server.go:341` (release).

The replacement is not a better seam. It is production calling the real function directly, and the
test standing up a real ephemeral instance — a real spawned process for a probe or an inventory, a
real codesigned bundle for a verifier. `own_test.go` already does this in 21 places, so the idiom
is in-repo.

A test that cannot be written without a seam is telling you the coverage belongs somewhere else —
delete it, or move it to the out-of-suite script. Do not keep it by widening the API.

## NOT seams — leave alone

- `internal/proc/posixspawn.go:25-32` — the purego trampolines (`posixSpawn`, `attrInit`,
  `attrSetFlags`, …). These are dynamically bound libc symbols; the indirection IS the production
  mechanism, not an injection point. Same for `internal/trust/csops.go:46` and
  `internal/trust/cms.go:293`, which return closures as ordinary functional style.
- `business.go:26` `attach` — the lane acquisition closure, used by production.
- `internal/wire/dial.go:10` — returns a dialer for production callers.
- Every `go func()` / `defer func()` — ordinary Go, not a seam.

The distinguishing test is not the type. It is whether production ever supplies a value. If only a
test does, the field should not exist.
ops.when: Before adding a func-typed field, an interface field, or an injectable parameter to a production type in daemonkit — and when closing out the de-fake sweep
